title: Momentum Anchors — personal commitment & weekly velocity log
content:
Purpose: a compact, forgiving scratchpad to keep small weekly commitments ("momentum anchors") and measure a few personal velocity signals. Not a full OKR doc — lightweight, for habitual check-ins and quick experiments.

How I use this: 1) pick 3 momentum anchors for the week (1 impact, 1 maintenance, 1 learning), 2) log daily micro-results, 3) score end-of-week velocity and note blockers. Reset next Monday.

---
Week window: 2026-03-02 — 2026-03-08  (example week)
Anchors (commitments):
- Impact: ship canary config for low-latency routing policy (INF-814) — deliver canary + rollout plan.
- Maintenance: reduce my PR review backlog to <= 6 open reviews and clear >= 8 review comments.
- Learning: finish reading "Efficient Inference Patterns" chapter and extract 3 small ops suggestions for runtime.

Daily micro-log (short, messy):
Mon: set up branch + initial canary config; opened PR (#1293). 1h pairing with Maya on rollout checklist.
Tue: blocked by infra creds; pinged infra SL. Did 2 PR reviews (d3, d7). Read 20% of chapter, noted caching idea.
Wed: infra returned; integrated canary. Ran a smoke with sample traffic; latency stable near baseline. Posted notes to #canary.
Thu: iterated on rollback metrics; wrote small alert doc. Reviewed 3 PRs. Spent 30m extracting ops suggestion drafts.
Fri: merged canary PR; smoke run across regions. Cleaned review backlog to 5. Quick retro with Eliot: rollout steps ambiguous around k8s HPA.

Velocity scoring (0–10 each):
- Impact progress: 8/10 (canary merged, rollout plan documented, still need runbook polish)
- Maintenance: 7/10 (backlog reduced to target but a couple reviews linger)
- Learning: 5/10 (chapter partially read; one clear ops suggestion captured)
Overall weekly velocity: 20/30 -> "steady"

Blockers / notes to self:
- Locking on infra creds took too long; escalate earlier next time (create shadow ticket when blocked > 8h).
- Pair earlier with SRE for HPA-related rollback testing; don't assume default HPA will behave under burst.
- Reduce meeting time Friday mornings by 30m to preserve deep block for rollouts.

Micro-experiments (hypothesis -> metric -> result):
1) Hypothesis: moving canary sample to 5% from 10% reduces noise in latency SLO signal without slowing detection. Metric: time-to-detect SLO degradation. Result: preliminary—detection window increased by ~20% but fewer false positives.
2) Hypothesis: triage window for reviews (set aside 45m/day) increases PR throughput. Metric: number of reviews completed per day. Result: +25% on days I block time.

Action items for next week:
- Finalize runbook: add explicit HPA & failure scenarios (owner: me).
- Automate smoke run: small script that runs 3-region check and uploads to canary dashboard.
- Schedule 45m review block M/W/F and evaluate after two weeks.
- Finish remaining 40% of the chapter and write short note with 3 actionable ops ideas.

Retrospective (quick):
What went well: got a canary out and merged in the same week; backlog management improved.
What to improve: quicker unblock handling; clearer pre-flight checklist with SRE.

Loose ideas / future anchors (seed list):
- Small habit: daily 15m "read & capture" before lunch for 4 days.
- Personal metric: measure average PR time-to-first-review (target < 24h).
- Work experiment: try canary at 2% for high-sensitivity SLOs and compare.

Questions / unresolved:
- Is there a standard SRE-owned baseline for HPA behaviour we should reference? (ask sre-runbooks)
- Can on-call playbook include a quick link to the canary rollback snippet? (file a small PR)

Notes to self (unfiltered):
- Keep the doc short. If anything needs formalizing, move to a dedicated Confluence page and link it from here.
- This doc is intentionally messy — it exists to force a 5–10 minute check-in ritual.

Template (copy for next week):
- Week window: YYYY-MM-DD — YYYY-MM-DD
- 3 anchors (impact / maintenance / learning)
- Daily micro-log (bullet brief)
- Velocity scoring 0–10 each, tally
- Key blockers + actions
- 2 micro-experiments (hypothesis -> metric -> result)
- 3 action items for next week
- Quick retro bullets

End of file.
